lines.text: We came up out of the tunnels into a Lowmarket cellar an hour before dawn. Seven of us. Ash was not one of them.
His thread had gone quiet in the dark behind us. Not snapped, the way Dunn's had. Just quiet. I kept reaching for it, the way your tongue keeps finding a missing tooth.
He held a stair against a dozen Hounds. He can hold a tunnel. He'll come.
Nobody answered her. Nobody had to.
My hands were still black from the Tide I'd sent across the city. Nell held the left one. Oddly, it hurt less while she did.
At noon, every bell in Aldcrown began to ring at once.
People of Aldcrown. Three hundred years ago, a hollow-born froze the North. Do not imagine it cannot happen again.
Lucan Varr, the boy you laughed at as a zero, is hollow-born. The same kind that froze the North.
By His Majesty's own warrant, under His Majesty's own seal, he is named a traitor to the realm.
The King's own seal. For a year, the Fourth Article had stood between me and every Measurer in Aldmere. Vance had simply walked around it.
Ten thousand crowns to whoever brings him to the Order. And a hundred a head for every member of his household. Children included.
It is... so ordered.
Ten thousand crowns, my lord. I've done the sums. It's an insult. You're worth forty, at the very least.
Thank you, Corvin.
And a hundred for me. A hundred! I kept House Corrow's books for twenty years.
By evening, my face was on every door in the city. The artist had never seen me. I looked like a worried goat.
Every gate is shut, my lord. Every barge is searched. And there are Hounds in the Lowmarket.
Then let them search. Nobody down here can read a poster, my lord. And nobody down here would, if they could.
She had carried stone for my aqueduct. Her thread was warm and stubborn, like a coal that won't go out.
That night I thought about the woman under the cathedral. Subject E. Greyhollow. Taken fifteen winters ago.
She had known my name. I had promised to come back for her. Now every Hound in Aldcrown stood between us.
You'll go back for her. I know you. But not tonight, Lucan. And not from a cellar.
Just after midnight, someone knocked on the cellar door. Three slow knocks. Wren had an arrow on the string before the third.
The figure at the top of the steps pushed back her hood. It was the King's own niece.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and ten, coming soon.
